svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The liver and its blood supply."], [1, "Blood from the gut, rich in absorbed glucose and amino acids, enters through the hepatic portal vein."], [4, "The hepatic artery brings oxygenated blood."], [6, "After insulin, liver cells convert excess glucose to glycogen; excess amino acids are deaminated to urea."], [9.5, "Processed blood leaves in the hepatic vein to the vena cava; urea travels to the kidneys."], [12, "Bile made in the liver is stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum to emulsify fats."]]
svg.title: The liver
svg.desc: The liver with the hepatic artery, hepatic portal vein and hepatic vein, gall bladder and bile duct to the duodenum, with animated blood and bile flow and a list of liver functions.
svg.text: The liver: blood supply, bile and functions
Simplified front view. Blue: deoxygenated. Red: oxygenated. Purple: blood from the gut.

g.data-info: The largest internal organ; its cells (hepatocytes) carry out hundreds of chemical reactions.
Stores and concentrates bile made by the liver.
Carries bile to the duodenum: bile emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid.
Absorbed food enters the blood and reaches the liver first in the hepatic portal vein.
Brings blood from the stomach and intestines, rich in absorbed glucose, amino acids and (sometimes) toxins, so the liver can process them first.
Brings oxygenated blood from the aorta.
Carries blood away from the liver to the vena cava.

Controls blood glucose, deaminates excess amino acids into urea, detoxifies alcohol and drugs, breaks down old red blood cells, stores iron and vitamins, and makes bile, plasma proteins and cholesterol.
g.text: • breaks down alcohol, drugs and hormones
• breaks down old red blood cells; stores iron
• stores vitamins A, D and B₁₂
